## 6. Pass lines (lock these before running; see rule 5)
Measure LCL criteria at the Service Delivery Point/POIB, which is bus 6255 (or 6018 in S4). Measure BESS criteria at the POIB, and also report the high side of the main transformer.
**BESS (ERCOT NOG 2.9.1.1 Table B and 2.6.2.1; NERC PRC-029-1 Table 2 and Table 3; IEEE 2800-2022 cl. 7 as adopted by NOG 2.9.1(2)):**
- B1 No trip and no momentary cessation while V(t) stays inside Table B: V>1.20 may trip; 1.10<V≤1.20 for 1.0 s; 0.90–1.10 continuous; 0.70≤V<0.90 for 6.0 s; 0.50≤V<0.70 for 3.0 s; 0.25≤V<0.50 for 1.2 s; 0.095625≤V<0.25 for (V+0.084375)/0.5625 s; V<0.095625 for 0.32 s. Times add up over a 10 s window.
- B2 Active power returns to its pre-disturbance level (or the available level) within ≤1.0 s after POIB voltage returns to 0.90–1.10 pu (NOG 2.9.1.1(4); PRC-029-1 R2.5).
- B3 Reactive current is injected throughout the mandatory region (PRC-029-1 R2.2). The sign is checked every step.
- B4 Frequency: no trip for 58.8–61.2 Hz (continuous), 61.2–61.6 Hz for 540 s, 61.6–61.8 Hz for 299 s, 58.4–58.8 Hz for 540 s, 57.0–58.4 Hz for 299 s (NOG 2.6.2.1). PRC-029-1 Table 3 (299 s outside 58.8–61.2 Hz) is also met within this. No trip on a ROCOF ≤ 5 Hz/s.
**LCL (ERCOT NOG 2.15 and 2.6.4, from NOGRR282, effective 08-01-2026):**
- L1 Stays connected inside Table A: V>1.20 may trip; 1.10<V≤1.20 for 1.0 s; 0.90–1.10 continuous; 0.80≤V<0.90 for 2.0 s; 0.50≤V<0.80 for 0.5 s; 0.35≤V<0.50 for 0.25 s; V<0.35 for 0.15 s. Cooling load may trip below 0.35 pu. Use a cooling share of 25% of LCL MW (an assumption; see the plan).
- L2 For dips that stay above 0.8 pu and recover above 0.9 pu within 2 s: the LCL keeps consuming, and is back to ≥90% of pre-disturbance P within 2 s of V>0.9 pu.
- L3 For dips below 0.8 pu: the LCL is back to ≥90% of pre-disturbance P within 2 s of V>0.9 pu. If a load-transfer scheme is modeled, it starts returning within 0.25 s and reaches ≥90% within 0.5 s.
- L4 LCL current ≤150% of its maximum normal current, for ≤0.5 s, during any undervoltage.
- L5 Survives six sags within 90 s (T6) without lockout (NOG 2.15(7)).
- L6 Frequency (2.6.4 Table A): 58.8–61.2 Hz continuous; 57.5–58.8 and 61.2–63.0 Hz for 299 s; P within 10% of pre-disturbance during these deviations.
**System (ERCOT Planning Guide 4.1.1.4–4.1.1.6; NERC PRC-024-4 Attachments 1–2 for synchronous units):**
- Y1 All buses >100 kV recover to ≥0.90 pu within 5 s after clearing (P1-type cases T1, T2, T3, T5) or 10 s (T4, T6).
- Y2 Oscillations between 0.2 and 2 Hz damp at ≥3% (Prony or matrix-pencil fit on the 230/500 kV angle differences; report the fit window).
- Y3 No loss of synchronism (COI-referenced angle separation <180°) and no generator outside the PRC-024-4 ERCOT no-trip boundaries. Frequency: ≥61.8 Hz instantaneous; ≥61.6 Hz for 30 s; ≥60.6 Hz for 540 s; ≤59.4 Hz for 540 s; ≤58.4 Hz for 30 s; ≤58.0 Hz for 2 s; ≤57.5 Hz instantaneous. Voltage: ≥1.20 pu 0 s; ≥1.175 pu 0.2 s; ≥1.15 pu 0.5 s; ≥1.10 pu 1.0 s; <0.45 pu 0.15 s; <0.65 pu 0.30 s; <0.75 pu 2.0 s; <0.90 pu 3.0 s.
- Y4 For T8, the frequency nadir is >59.3 Hz, so no first-stage UFLS (NOG 2.6.1 Table 1).
- Y5 For T9/T10, the frequency peak is <60.6 Hz, and 230/500 kV voltages are ≤1.05 pu after 10 s (PG 4.1.1.4(1)(b)).
Verdict for each case and criterion: PASS / FAIL / NOT APPLICABLE, with the margin (minimum distance to the boundary in pu or seconds).
